_comment: Release manifest. Every Hub with update checks on fetches this file and compares its own version against `version`. Bump it as part of cutting a release, not before - the harness pins it equal to package.json so a manifest that lies about the current release cannot ship.
notes: 2.45.4: on a phone the Dispatch timeline no longer jumps back to the top while you scroll down it - the plan refresh rebuilt it every few seconds and only kept your place left to right, so the last printers were out of reach. 2.45.3: the Dispatch timeline can be moved through time from anywhere - it is now bounded to the window height with the ruler pinned at its top and its own scrollbar always in view, the tools row has earlier and later buttons, dragging the lanes pans, and the arrow keys work once the timeline has focus; before, the horizontal scrollbar sat below the last printer. 2.45.2: the Models tab no longer dims every few seconds during a rescan - the background poll that keeps the count line moving used to fade the grid and block taps for the length of each request; only a load you asked for (a search, a designer, Show more, Rescan) does that now. 2.45.1: the Models tab no longer flashes and jumps while you scroll it during a rescan - the page used to rebuild every card every four seconds while the folder walk ran (thumbnails re-requested, color chips reset and refilled); now it redraws only when the cards themselves changed, and the chips row keeps a fixed one-line height so filling it in cannot push the cards below it. 2.45.0: the Hub takes one snapshot of the farm per pass and every part of it (the live page, Dispatch, the print-start watcher, the fleet events) reads from that one, so nine printers no longer get polled four ways; the Dispatch timeline keeps moving while the tab is open and re-reads the plan every minute; pause, resume and cancel show a spinner and refuse a second tap until the printer answers; a settings save that fails on a slow share says so instead of Saved; config.json is checked at startup (a wrong type names the key, an unknown key only warns, a PowerShell BOM no longer drops the file to defaults); finished push jobs and thumbnail metadata no longer pile up in memory; Sign out everywhere and a trusted proxies field join the Settings auth card; overnight finishes are planned as a queue of bed clears five minutes apart instead of three starts at once; GET /healthz for a watchdog and a nightly backup of the state files into a backups folder beside them (seven days kept); and a GitHub Actions workflow runs the test harness on Linux and Windows for every push and refuses a release tag that does not match the code. 3MF Explorer 1.7.1 ships alongside: quarantine is undoable from History, Settings has the archive interval and saves even while the library drive is offline, search is debounced, moves across drives copy and verify before deleting, config.json is checked with the same rules, /healthz and nightly database backups, and the same CI. 2.44.1: two fixes from the first phone test of 2.44.0 - the button that reveals Rescan and Folder on a narrow screen now shows (a style-order slip kept it hidden), and the rescanning line counts folders walked as well as files found, so it moves from the first second instead of sitting at 0 while the walk crosses folders with no 3MF. 2.44.0: the Models tab works on a phone - the designer list shows the biggest designers plus a search box instead of hundreds of chips, the shelf opens newest first, the gcode sidebar folds away behind a Library button on narrow screens, and Convert to U1, Link gcode, Attributes, Rename and Delete are all reachable from a card's menu on touch. Cards carry their project's filament colors as a strip along the top, printed counts and the filed mark sit on the picture, and Today / This week dividers run down the newest view. Designer names can be renamed or merged from the Folder panel without touching a file, and folder names that cannot be a designer group as (unsorted). Dispatch learns how long each file really takes on each printer and plans with that, keeps the plan ready and pushes it to the page as it changes, holds a copy in flight from the moment you start it, and every planned block now says why it is on that printer and what the runners-up would have cost. An expired sign-in sends you to the sign-in page instead of showing Fleet unreachable; the Cloudflare tunnel relaunches itself after a crash when autostart is on, downloads one pinned cloudflared release and checks it before every launch, and the tunnel and the proxy sign-in modes can no longer be on at the same time. Nothing polls while the tab is hidden, a push no longer freezes the other printer cards, and a printer that never accepted a connection says could not connect instead of stalled. 3MF Explorer 1.7.0 ships alongside: the library list is compressed and a tenth of the size, scan problems show on the page, every destructive button survives a server error, and scans are faster on network shares. 2.43.0: printers keep their identity when you reorder them in Settings - Dispatch claims, maintenance and pins follow the machine, not its place in the list. A copy that finishes while the Hub is off still counts, a cancelled or failed print frees its printer and keeps the copy owed with a notice on the job, and completions match the exact file and printer type. Copies between printers and into the library can't hang. Sign-in hardening: changing the password signs out older sessions (everyone signs in once after this update), and login lockouts count per visitor through the tunnel. On the Models tab, an Orca saved line goes away once its gcode is in Dispatch. 3MF Explorer 1.6.1 ships alongside: Delete on a network drive goes to quarantine (Windows has no Recycle Bin there), no move ever replaces an existing file, and other web pages can't send it requests. 2.42.0: safety fixes. The Models tab never lists, renames or deletes the U1 template files (u1_template*.3mf, filament_types.3mf). Sending a file to a printer that stops answering now fails after 30 s instead of hanging, and the file can be renamed or deleted again; every printer command in the print pipeline has a time limit. A job you move to a printer by hand stays there after a Hub restart, and lowering a Dispatch job's count to the copies already printed finishes it. 2.41.0: Print on best printer - select a file and the Hub picks an idle printer that already has every color it needs loaded, tells you which one, and gives you five seconds to cancel before it sends; if nothing fits, it says which printer came closest and what it's missing, and when that's only a color or two you can send it there anyway - it shows which loaded roll stands in for each missing color first. Head mapping now weighs every arrangement instead of going first-come, so a loaded color can't be taken by one that doesn't match anything. Open in Orca with these settings - on a model's Settings panel, one button opens a copy of the 3MF in Orca with the AI's suggested settings already loaded, marked as changes you can undo; your own file is never touched and the copy cleans itself up after three days. 3MF Explorer 1.5.0 ships alongside: archive files you haven't printed in a year. Right-click Archive or Restore, an 'Include archive' checkbox next to the search box, and an automatic monthly run. Every run can be undone from History. 2.40.2: the head auto-mapping matches material before color, so a PETG part no longer lands on a PLA roll of the same color, and the mapping row warns if the head you pick holds a different material (thanks Florent). A file that only lives on a printer can now be copied into the Hub library from Send to. Spoolman write-back (opt-in, off until you turn it on) records each print's grams in Spoolman. Colors set from the Hub keep their material on the printer. Print requests from 3MF Explorer match by place in the library, not by drive letter. The Dispatch timeline has a key for its badges, the file list's Send to strip wraps on small screens, and 3MF Explorer 1.4.1 ships alongside the Hub. Unloading filament after a print is in this build but switched off for now while we check whether it causes nozzle clogs. 2.40.1: the Logbook's entries are compact cards again (they were picking up the page layout's padding), its links match the Hub's colors, and the README has new pictures of print requests, the Logbook, Timelapses and 3MF Explorer. 2.40.0: print requests from 3MF Explorer (Mark for print there, the Hub queues one print when its gcode is saved), Link gcode by hand, Open in Orca links the right file, timelapses saved to a folder you pick (off until you turn them on in Settings) that no longer freeze on one old picture six minutes into a print, Dispatch refuses to queue the same file twice (raise the count instead), and 3MF Explorer now ships alongside the Hub. 2.39.0: fixes 2.34's timelapse capture losing most of a print. The Hub restarts several times a day for unrelated reasons, and until now a restart mid-print always started a brand-new, empty capture for that printer - every frame from before the restart was silently abandoned on disk. Most timelapses were only ever showing the last few minutes of a print, which is why a print that ran for hours could turn into a video where nothing visibly changes. The Hub now saves its place after every captured frame and a restart resumes the SAME capture where it left off, so frames accumulate across restarts instead of resetting. 2.38.0: Convert to U1 on the Models tab (issue #5) - a MakerWorld or Bambu project becomes a U1 copy that keeps the designer's prime tower, walls, infill and supports. 2.37.0: a Logbook for every printer - what went wrong, what fixed it, and a maintenance schedule by print hours or days. Pauses and errors the printer reports, and printers you take out of service, are logged by themselves; what's due shows on the printer card and can ping your phone. 2.36.0: the planner stops leaving printers idle - no more waiting until midnight for a job to 'fit', and running prints no longer draw twice on the timeline. Models: format folders like U1 and prusa-format are no longer treated as designers, Random shows every model before repeating one and mixes designers, and Rename/Attributes/Delete moved behind a corner menu. Fixed: pressing Open in Orca could freeze the whole Hub for up to half an hour on a network share. 2.35.0: fixes the freeze reported in issue #4 - with several cameras streaming, the page could stop updating after a few minutes; a tile now asks for one frame at a time and the Hub grabs a printer's frame once for everyone waiting. On screens 1500px and wider the dashboard, Dispatch, Models and Match views use the room, so four U1s fit in one row on a 4K monitor. Older releases: see docs/CHANGELOG.md.
